Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i have been using the same browser extension on my home laptop and the computer I use at work, and the preference screen is where I decide how much it should interrupt me. I want the extension to be useful when I ask for it, but I do not want its controls to take over the browser. I usually prefer a compact button in the toolbar, rather than a panel opening by itself when a page loads. The extension currently has a toolbar icon, a side panel, notifications, and a small status mark on supported pages, so I am thinking about how those pieces should relate, not asking to remove all of them.

The first preference I look for is whether the extension is active on a particular site. I would like that choice to be easy to find and easy to reverse, because I sometimes need the feature for a page and sometimes want to read without it. A site switch should apply to the current site, not silently become a setting for every site. I also want a clear difference between pausing the extension temporarily and turning it off for a site. If I pause it, I expect the pause to end when I choose, not because I happen to close the current tab. If I disable it for a site, that site should remain disabled until I change that choice.

I do not need the extension to display a notice every time it runs. A small status mark is enough for me, as long as it can be recognized without taking up much space. Notifications are different: I would like to control them separately from the status mark, since a visible mark can be useful while repeated pop-ups are distracting. I occasionally miss a notification that contains a real change, though, so I would rather not have one universal switch that treats every message in exactly the same way. A setting for important notices and another for routine notices would be easier for me to understand, if the extension has those types of messages.

1. The toolbar button should open the extension controls when I select it; it should not open the side panel automatically.
2. The side panel should be something I can open when I want more room to review the current page. I would prefer it to remember its last width, but not to cover the browser's main controls.
3. The status mark should remain optional and separate from notifications. If there is no useful status to show on a page, I do not need a blank mark there.
4. The extension should offer a simple way to pause on the current site, with a clear indication of whether it is paused or disabled for that site.

I use the same preferences in different situations, and I do not want a change on one device to surprise me on the other. If I enable sync, I want only the extension preferences to follow my account; saved page content should not be included in that choice. If sync is off, I expect the choices to stay with the browser profile where I made them. This matters because I sometimes use a work computer that has a separate browser profile, and I do not want its extension settings to become mixed with the settings on my home laptop. I might keep sync off most of the time, but I would like the choice to be visible rather than buried in a general account page.

The wording on the preference screen should make the effect of a control clear before I select it. I have seen labels such as “quiet mode” that sound appealing but do not tell me whether they hide the status mark, stop notifications, or both. A short explanation beside a setting would be more useful than a long description in a separate help page. I do not need every preference to have a paragraph under it, and I would rather see a few precise lines than a wall of text. For example, “Pause on this site until I turn it back on” says more to me than a vague label like “temporary.”

I also want the screen to distinguish preferences that affect every site from those that affect only the site I am currently viewing. If I change a general notification preference while looking at a page, that should not make it seem as though I changed the site's individual setting too. The site-specific controls can be grouped together, with the general display and notification controls in another area. I would not put the sync switch next to the pause control, because they have different effects and I could easily mistake one for the other when making a quick change.

There are a few details I am less certain about. I usually keep the side panel narrow, but I might want it wider when I am reviewing a page with a long list of items. Remembering its width would help, provided the panel still stays within the browser window on a smaller screen. I also prefer that the extension remember whether I last opened the panel, but I do not want it to reopen by itself on the next page or after restarting the browser. Those are separate things to me: remembering a size is convenient, while restoring an open panel can feel like an interruption.

When I review the preferences later, I want to be able to tell which choices are global, which are for the current site, and which depend on sync being enabled. The controls can stay compact, but the labels should not make those distinctions hard to notice. I would use a short site name near the site-specific controls and a separate heading for the general preferences. If sync is disabled, its status should still be shown in that area, so I can understand why the settings are staying with this browser profile.
